title: High-Quality Ex Vivo Soft Tissue Imaging with Compact MRI Systems
author: Litwak, Sarabia, et al.
materials: C57BL/6J mice (The Jackson Laboratory, cat. no. 000664)

Phosphate‐buffered saline (PBS; pH 7.4; Gibco, Fisher Scientific, cat. no. 10010001)
Fluorinert FC‐70 (Millipore Sigma, cat. no. F9880‐25 ml)

steps.title: Perfuse animal before dissection
steps.instruction: Perfuse the animal using a standard vascular perfusion method to improve tissue quality before dissecting the target soft tissue.

steps.title: Dissect tissue sample
steps.instruction: Dissect the animal to obtain the desired ex vivo soft tissue sample for subsequent processing.

steps.title: Soak sample in Gd‑DTPA
steps.instruction: Place the dissected tissue in a solution of Gd‑DTPA and incubate overnight to allow contrast agent uptake.

steps.title: Embed sample in Fluorinert
steps.instruction: Transfer the Gd‑DTPA‑soaked tissue into Fluorinert (a perfluorinated compound without movable protons) ensuring the sample is fully immersed and immobilized for MRI.

steps.title: Store embedded sample
steps.instruction: Keep the Fluorinert‑embedded sample under appropriate storage conditions (e.g., refrigerated) until imaging or future use.

steps.title: Prepare 5% agarose gel (alternate)
steps.instruction: Dissolve agarose to a final concentration of 5 % (w/v) in the chosen buffer, heat until completely melted; this preparation takes approximately 10 minutes.

steps.title: Embed sample in agarose (alternate)
steps.instruction: After Gd‑DTPA soaking, place the tissue into the liquid 5 % agarose gel and allow it to solidify, noting that agarose contains movable protons and may increase background noise and be difficult to remove later.

steps.title: Acquire MRI images
steps.instruction: Scan the embedded sample with a compact MRI system; the optimized scan time is approximately 13 hours.
